readings: Compute each film `rating`'s average `length`, ignoring missing lengths. As the baseline, take the average length over all films, with each film counting equally. Keep the ratings whose average length is above that baseline. Among those ratings, take the mean of their average lengths and keep only the ratings that are above that mean too. Return one row with: the mean of the remaining ratings' average lengths, the mean amount by which they exceed the baseline, and the mean amount by which they exceed the kept ratings' mean. Do not round anything.
queries:
WITH rating_averages AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(length) AS avg_length
  FROM film
  GROUP BY rating
),
baseline AS (
  SELECT AVG(length) AS avg_length
  FROM film
),
above_baseline AS (
  SELECT ra.rating, ra.avg_length
  FROM rating_averages AS ra
  CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
  WHERE ra.avg_length > b.avg_length
),
kept_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_length) AS avg_length
  FROM above_baseline
)
SELECT
  AVG(ab.avg_length) AS mean_length,
  AVG(ab.avg_length - b.avg_length) AS mean_above_baseline,
  AVG(ab.avg_length - km.avg_length) AS mean_above_kept_mean
FROM above_baseline AS ab
CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
CROSS JOIN kept_mean AS km
WHERE ab.avg_length > km.avg_length
